rich_summary: On the night of Victor and Elizabeth’s wedding, a violent storm rises over the lake, mirroring Victor’s dread of the Creature’s threat: “I shall be with you on your wedding night.” Expecting a personal attack, Victor arms himself and patrols the inn, but the danger falls instead on Elizabeth. Her sudden scream leads Victor to the room where he finds her murdered, bearing the mark of the Creature’s grasp. The monster briefly appears at the window, grinning and pointing at the corpse before escaping across the lake. The tragedy cascades: Victor’s father dies from the shock, Victor is imprisoned as a madman, and his life collapses into isolation. Emerging from grief and confinement, he resolves on a single purpose—revenge—and begins the obsessive pursuit of the being he created.

highlight_spans.why: The eerie lakeside arrival and gathering storm create a lonely, foreboding landscape that sets the chapter’s fatal mood.
Elizabeth’s scream and Victor’s realization mark the pivotal moment where the Creature’s wedding-night threat is fulfilled.
Victor’s discovery of Elizabeth’s lifeless body is one of the novel’s most emotionally devastating images.
The Creature’s appearance at the moonlit window—grinning and pointing at the corpse—is a chilling confrontation between creator and creation.
Victor’s declaration that revenge is now the ‘devouring and only passion’ of his soul marks the transformation from grieving husband to relentless hunter.

top_scenes.scene_text: A storm-lashed lakeshore at night as Victor stands tense outside the inn, hand hidden on a pistol while clouds race across the moon.
Victor discovering Elizabeth’s lifeless body across the bridal bed, moonlight entering through the window as curtains and hair fall across her pale face.
The Creature framed in the open window by yellow moonlight, grinning and pointing at Elizabeth’s corpse while Victor fires a pistol and the monster leaps toward the dark lake.
